teams.heading: Fiji concede more than they score across their last 11 matches
teams.body: In their last 11 fixtures, Fiji have scored 315 points. Across that same 11-game window, the team has conceded 326 points. Fiji have averaged 28.6 points scored per match over those 11 games, while conceding 29.6 points per game in the same period. The biggest win of this 11-match span came in September 2025, when they beat Canada 63-10 at home during the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage.

teams.heading: L'Équipe reports Thomas Ramos set for shock Toulouse exit to Racing 92
teams.body: France full-back Thomas Ramos is reportedly considering a "sensational" departure from Toulouse after the 2027 Rugby World Cup, with Racing 92 his likely destination. According to L’Équipe, the move to Paris could see the France star transition to a primary fly-half role, a position he has frequently occupied at Test level but rarely for his club. Ramos has made 200 appearances for Toulouse, winning four league titles and two Champions Cups during an era of sustained domestic dominance.

teams.heading: Former Ireland Lock Ryan Caldwell Opens Up On Life After Rugby
teams.body: Former Ireland international Ryan Caldwell has shared a candid account of his transition from the professional game to his current role as a meditation teacher. In a recent interview, the 41-year-old discussed his journey through injury, addiction, and depression following a playing career that saw him represent Ulster, Bath, and Exeter. Caldwell, who is preparing to release an autobiography, detailed how he moved past his playing days to find peace and now supports others through breathwork and meditation techniques.

teams.heading: Tom Rogers targets Wales recall following summer move to the Ospreys
teams.body: After securing a move to the Ospreys this summer, Tom Rogers is focused on forcing his way back into the international fold. The versatile back, who famously scored a hat-trick against New Zealand in Cardiff, has not featured for his country since that record-breaking performance. Rogers admitted he was disappointed with his recent outing for the Barbarians, stating, "I just need to play well with the Ospreys and show I deserve to be in the squad" under new coach Steve Tandy.

lead.why: The story provides a direct look at a player's ambition to reclaim a spot in the squad under the new coaching regime.

teams.heading: Australia makes nine changes to starting XV for Mendoza rematch
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss has overhauled his side for the return fixture in Mendoza, making nine alterations to the team that won in San Salvador de Jujuy. Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Len Ikitau reunite in the midfield, while Ben Donaldson starts at flyhalf for the first time in two years. Australia aims to secure a historic two-Test series sweep on Argentine soil. Kiss noted, "We’ve brought in some fresh bodies alongside some existing combinations as we continue to look to build Test experience."

lead.why: The Wallabies have made nine changes for the second Test in Mendoza, providing the most significant pre-match news.

teams.heading: Ardie Savea ruled out of fourth test after suffering shoulder injury
teams.body: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea will miss next Saturday’s fourth test in Baltimore after sustaining a shoulder injury during yesterday’s 29-24 defeat at FNB Stadium. Savea, who scored two first-half tries, left the field in the 30th minute and will not travel with the squad to the United States. His absence creates a significant leadership and tactical void for Dave Rennie’s side as they look to salvage a 2-2 series draw in the final outing of the rivalry.

lead.why: The report confirms a significant injury blow to captain Ardie Savea ahead of the final test.
